Simulxalive · submit

Put a paper
in the queue.

One socket per way a reference can arrive. Paste it, say what it bears on, and the page builds the submission envelope. Nothing here writes to the corpus — a person accepts it, or it does not enter.

1 · the reference

Paste it whole.

A bare id or a full link both work, and a DOI buried in a publisher URL is found. 10.1038/s41562-024-01882-z · arXiv:2303.11436 · W2741809807

Routed to waiting Key —
2 · the citation

What the paper actually says it is.

Nothing fills these in for you. The layer makes no network call and will not manufacture a citation from an identifier, so a draft missing any of them is refused at the gate rather than completed by guesswork.

3 · what it bears on

Tag it against the taxonomy.

The 28 constructs, as they are grouped in data/axes.json. Scores are not set here — convergence and robustness are codings argued by a person against the rubric, never a submission field.

Domain

Amber is human, violet is machine — a bridge paper measures both sides in one study.

4 · the envelope

Hand it to the review gate.

This page is static, so it does not write data/inbox.json itself. It builds the envelope; Python replays it, re-derives the key, checks it against all 61 sources and the queue, and refuses what it cannot verify.


    

      
      
      
    

    
Then, in the repository:

    
python3 tools/ingest.py submit --json - < submission.json

    

      
    

  


  

    

      Never invent a number
      
Every figure in the atlas traces to a cited paper or to a measurement row from our own
      harness. A socket that filled in a plausible title would be the fastest way to break that.

    

    

      Codings are not findings
      
Convergence and robustness are our judgements against a published rubric. They are argued
      in review, not typed into a form.

    

    

      A person decides
      
Submissions stage in an inbox. Accepting one records who submitted it, who accepted it and
      which socket it came through.
